summary: Say the counting numbers in order, starting at 1 and going all the way to 20.
Count backward from 5 down to 1, like a countdown before a rocket takes off.
Say which number comes next when counting, for any number up to 10.
Notice when someone skips or repeats a number while counting, and fix their own counting slips.
Use the order words first to fifth, like picking out the fourth bear in a row.
Count up to 10 things, saying one number for each thing and the numbers in the right order.
Count up to 10 things set out in a line, touching each once, and say how many there are.
See how many are in a small group, up to 5, straight away without counting one by one.
Count out exactly the number of things asked for, up to 10, like handing over five blocks.
Say how many there are now when one is added to or taken from a group of up to 4.
Compare groups of up to 10 things and say which have more, which have fewer, or that they're equal.
Know some of the written numbers from 0 to 10 by sight and say their names.
Count a group of 1 to 5 things and match it to the written number that says how many.
Show a number from 0 to 5 by writing it, drawing that many things or setting out objects.
Sort things into groups by how they look, such as by size or by shape.
Spot a simple repeating pattern, copy it, and say or add what comes next.
Make up a repeating pattern of their own and point out the part that repeats.
Act out small adding and taking-away problems with objects, with answers of 5 or less.
Compare up to five things by height or weight, and put them in order from least to most.
Use words like taller, heavier, shortest and biggest to compare two or more things.
Find how long something is by lining up other objects, like blocks, along it.
Name circles, triangles, squares and rectangles, whatever their size or which way they're turned.
Describe and compare shapes by how many sides and corners they have and how long the sides are.
Find flat and solid shapes in the world around them, like a ball, a can or a cone.
Build shapes out of smaller parts, like two triangle blocks put together to make a square.
Pick shapes and slide, turn or flip them so they match a picture or a model.
Understand and use words for where things are and which way to move: on top, beside, below.
